name: Longest run of consecutive integers with distinct divisor counts below 10^10
description: construct() -> {'start': s, 'length': k} with s >= 1, 1 <= k <= 40 and s + k - 1 <= 10^10. The divisor counts tau(s), ..., tau(s + k - 1) must be pairwise distinct (exact factorization). Maximize k; the optimum is 14 (first run at 1745175039). Runs ending below 10^10 have at most 14 terms (first at 1745175039), so the task recovers such a run.

sources.locator: P. Erdős and L. Mirsky, The Distribution of Values of the Divisor Function d(n) (1952). Crossref record inspected; Erdős Problem #945 page inspected (Erdős and Mirsky proved (log x)^(1/2)/log log x << F(x) << exp(O((log x)^(1/2)/log log x)); Beker improved the upper bound; Guy B18). OEIS A048892 inspected: the first run of 14 consecutive integers with distinct divisor counts starts at 1745175039 and the first run of 15 at 31287652672 > 10^10, so F(10^10) = 14. Runs ending below 10^10 have at most 14 terms (first at 1745175039), so the task recovers such a run.
